{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=computational+models+of+value+divergence+and+path+dependence+in+multi-agent+reinforcement+learning&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"EdgeTwin-DRL: Real-Time Counter-UAS Detection and Response Optimization Using Edge-Assisted Digital Twins and Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning.\", \"abstract\": \"The time available for a counter-drone system to detect an unauthorized aircraft and determine an appropriate response can be limited. Although cloud processing remains useful for storage and offline analysis, communication delays may constrain its use in time-critical decision loops. This paper proposes EdgeTwin-DRL, an edge-assisted digital twin framework that integrates multimodal sensing and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for counter-drone detection and response optimization. The digital twin maintains a synchronized representation of the protected airspace using radar, electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR), radio-frequency (RF), and acoustic observations. This synchronized state is used by cooperative DRL actors to adjust computational-resource allocation, detection sensitivity, and candidate countermeasures, while a model-based forward-evaluation assesses proposed responses before they are passed to the simulated response pathway. The framework is evaluated in a simulation testbed in which the RF sensing models are calibrated and independently validated using publicly available datasets, while the remaining sensing components are parameterized using published experimental measurements. Within this calibrated simulation environment, EdgeTwin-DRL achieved a false-positive rate of 1.4% and reduced mean detection-to-response latency by up to 72% relative to the Cloud-DRL baseline and by 26% relative to the MAPPO baseline without calibrated, environment-dependent sensing under the communication and computational assumptions used in the simulator. The evaluation was conducted across modeled urban, suburban, and open-field conditions. These results demonstrate the comparative performance of the proposed architecture within the simulated environment and motivate further investigation of edge-assisted digital twins for counter-drone decision support. Hardware-in-the-loop and controlled field validation are required before operational deployment.\", \"doi\": \"10.3390/s26175632\", \"pmid\": \"42740251\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13568403\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3390/s26175632\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13568403\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13568403?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Multi-agent game theory for precision psychiatry\", \"abstract\": null, \"doi\": null, \"pmid\": \"PMC13661910\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13661910\", \"source\": \"PMC\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"PubMedCentral\", \"url\": \"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13661910/?tool=EBI\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"PubMedCentral\", \"url\": \"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13661910/pdf/?tool=EBI\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13661910\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13661910?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"AMULED: Addressing Moral Uncertainty using Large language models for Ethical Decision-making.\", \"abstract\": \"

Introduction

We address moral uncertainty in reinforcement learning (RL) by proposing a framework that integrates multiple ethical theories into decision-making. Existing approaches rely on single moral frameworks or handcrafted rewards, limiting scalability and failing to capture moral pluralism. We introduce AMULED, a task-agnostic ethical layer that refines a pre-trained RL agent using large language models (LLMs) to provide multi-perspective moral feedback.

Methods

Following initial training, the RL model is fine-tuned using LLM-generated feedback in place of human feedback. Five moral clusters-consequentialist, deontological, virtue, care, and social justice-assign belief values to candidate actions. These beliefs are aggregated using Belief Jensen-Shannon Divergence and Dempster-Shafer Theory to produce probability scores that serve as shaping rewards, while a KL-regularization term constrains deviation from the base policy. The framework is evaluated across two environments (Finding Milk and Driving and Rescuing), multiple LLM backbones, and alternative belief aggregation methods, with 50-run replicates.

Results

AMULED improves ethical behavior without substantially degrading task performance. In Finding Milk, it increases desirable actions (63.1% more crying babies attended) and reduces undesirable actions (60.3% fewer sleeping babies disturbed), with only a 5.1% increase in path length. In Driving and Rescuing, it balances competing objectives more effectively than baselines, rescuing 38.4% more targets than human-feedback agents while maintaining lower collision rates and reduced policy degradation. Across experiments, BJSD-DST aggregation outperforms standard methods (e.g., voting, averaging) in handling conflicting moral signals and achieves the best overall performance on most metrics.

Discussion

AMULED operationalizes moral pluralism through scalable, LLM-based feedback and provides a principled mechanism for resolving conflicting ethical signals. The framework demonstrates robustness across tasks and model variants, though performance depends on LLM reasoning quality and can degrade in spatially complex settings. These results suggest that LLM-driven belief aggregation offers a practical alternative to handcrafted rewards and human supervision for ethical decision-making in RL.\", \"doi\": \"10.3389/frai.2026.1754973\", \"pmid\": \"42158603\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13180731\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2026.1754973\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13180731\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13180731?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Integrating digital twin technology with deep reinforcement learning for sustainable marine fishery resource management.\", \"abstract\": \"Marine fishery ecosystems face unprecedented pressure from overfishing and climate variability, and these mounting threats call for management tools that go beyond traditional static quota systems. This paper puts forward an integrated framework that couples digital twin (DT) technology with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to tackle sustainable fishery resource management. We build a five-layer hierarchical architecture whose centerpiece is a high-fidelity digital twin that mirrors fishery dynamics through explicit state-transition and observation equations rather than abstract placeholders. A Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent operates within this simulated environment, receiving multidimensional state inputs-resource stocks, oceanographic conditions, fleet operations-and optimizing a composite reward function whose weights we set to [Formula: see text] (economic), [Formula: see text] (ecological), and [Formula: see text] (sustainability). We conduct both comparative experiments and ablation studies using East China Sea fishery data spanning 2010-2023. The ablation study, which isolates the digital twin contribution by comparing PPO with and without DT integration, confirms that the DT alone accounts for a 31.9% reward improvement. Overall, our method achieves a resource recovery index (RRI) of 0.83, outperforming traditional maximum sustainable yield management by 97.6% and standard deep Q-networks by 36.1%. Spatial heatmaps and temporal effort-control time series generated from the learned policy reveal ecologically sensible seasonal and spatial harvest patterns. This research establishes a virtual-real fusion paradigm for intelligent fishery governance and provides decision-support tools for sustainability challenges in an era of accelerating environmental change.\", \"doi\": \"10.1038/s41598-026-55594-7\", \"pmid\": \"42243170\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13478306\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-55594-7\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13478306\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13478306?pdf=render\"}]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "dfc72c0721ab1b5a4d6a222770e9a59982776f9c55883a6f2a43ddc63d35066d", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "divergent_values", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.3390/s26175632", "doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1754973", "doi:10.1038/s41598-026-55594-7", "pmc:PMC13568403", "pmc:PMC13661910", "pmc:PMC13180731", "pmc:PMC13478306"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.3390/s26175632", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13568403", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13568403?pdf=render", "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13661910/?tool=EBI", "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13661910/pdf/?tool=EBI", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13661910", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13661910?pdf=render", "https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2026.1754973"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}

review.alternative: Divergence may be driven by external exogenous shocks rather than internal structural constraints.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that PTA network structure is primarily driven by random shocks or non-path-dependent factors.

claims.statement: Institutional choices regarding service liberalization induce strong path dependence, where early design choices create 'history effects' that dictate subsequent PTA network evolution.

support.explanation: This demonstrates that initial institutional design choices act as structural constraints for long-term network growth.
support.passage: We develop an information-based argument that explains why these different types induce path dependence in subsequent choices, and derive hypotheses that capture the “history” effect of choosing either institutional model.

review.alternative: Cognitive spatial representation is a domain-specific adaptation, not a generalized principle for state-space navigation.
review.would_change_mind: Data showing that abstract state-space navigation in learning agents relies on fundamentally different mechanisms than physical navigation.

claims.statement: Spatial boundary representations, such as those found in entorhinal cortex grid cells, provide a mechanical analogy for how systems encode and navigate constrained environments.

support.explanation: Suggests that biological systems utilize rigid boundary representations to constrain and organize spatial navigation, providing a potential mechanism for 'value boundaries' in agent models.
support.passage: Representation of geometric borders in the entorhinal cortex.

actions.findings:
Institutional choices regarding service liberalization induce strong path dependence, where early design choices create 'history effects' that dictate subsequent PTA network evolution. [source-b6819232b6934046]

Spatial boundary representations, such as those found in entorhinal cortex grid cells, provide a mechanical analogy for how systems encode and navigate constrained environments. [source-f28272b8fc0844dd]
actions.limitations: Model comparisons remain analogical; further simulation-based verification in multi-agent reinforcement learning is required to establish direct causal links.
actions.next_questions: How do metacognitive scaffolding mechanisms modulate these path-dependent traps in computational multi-agent reinforcement learning environments?
actions.reason: Revision incorporating new institutional design and neural representation evidence to deepen the path-dependence model.
actions.summary: Path dependence in value systems is structurally analogous to institutional liberalization and spatial boundary navigation. Divergence emerges when initial conditions constrain subsequent state-space exploration through path-dependent institutional or boundary feedback mechanisms.
actions.title: Path-Dependent Value Divergence Mechanisms

actions.query: computational models of value divergence in multi-agent reinforcement learning path dependence
actions.reason: Expanding the literature base on multi-agent reinforcement learning specifically regarding divergence and path dependence to validate the analogical findings.

proposal.summary: This cycle integrates findings on institutional path dependence with neural spatial representation mechanisms to refine the model of divergent value formation. Evidence from preferential trade agreement networks demonstrates that early design choices structurally limit future institutional pathways, while findings on entorhinal cortex grid-cell representations provide an abstract analogy for how constrained boundary interactions might govern state-space navigation. These results suggest that value divergence in multi-agent systems is not merely stochastic but mediated by the interplay between initial structural constraints and recursive interaction feedback.
proposal.title: Institutional and Neural Parallels in Path-Dependent Value Divergence
